title: CacheDyG: Decoupling Temporal Propagation for Efficient Dynamic Graph Learning
abstract: arXiv:2609.25814v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Dynamic graphs are widely used to model time-evolving relational systems in real-world applications. Dynamic graph neural networks provide an effective framework for capturing both structural dependencies and temporal dynamics in such data. However, they typically intertwine temporal graph propagation with every optimization epoch and often maintain large trainable representations for each node-time pair. This design repeatedly recomputes largely unchanged historical structures, leading to substantial training and parameter overhead. To address this critical issue, we propose CacheDyG, a Cache-refine framework for efficient Dynamic Graph learning. Specifically, it decouples temporal propagation from routine parameter updates by constructing a time-ordered temporal dependency cache that stores graph-aware node-time representations in non-trainable buffers. translated_title: CacheDyG：解耦时序传播以实现高效动态图学习
translated_abstract: 动态图被广泛用于建模现实世界应用中随时间演化的关系系统。动态图神经网络为捕捉此类数据中的结构依赖和时间动态提供了有效框架。然而，这些方法通常将时序图传播与每次优化迭代交织在一起，并且常常为每个节点-时间对维护大量可训练的表示。这种设计会反复重新计算基本不变的历史结构，导致巨大的训练和参数开销。为了解决这一关键问题，我们提出了CacheDyG，一个用于高效动态图学习的缓存-精炼框架。具体而言，它通过构建一个按时间排序的时序依赖缓存，将图感知的节点-时间表示存储在不可训练的缓冲区中，从而将时序传播与常规参数更新解耦。在标准训练迭代期间，CacheDyG从缓存中读取数据并仅更新……
tldr: CacheDyG通过构建按时间排序的时序依赖缓存，将时序图传播与参数更新解耦，避免重复计算历史结构，从而大幅降低动态图神经网络的训练和参数开销。
en_tdlr: CacheDyG decouples temporal graph propagation from parameter updates by constructing a time-ordered temporal dependency cache, avoiding redundant recomputation of historical structures and significantly reducing training and parameter overhead in dynamic graph learning.
